- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

message.reasoning:
I need to decide on a Monopoly action.

I have $841 and three properties. p1 owns a full pink monopoly and $795. p3 has a dark blue set with one house each and only $222 cash.

p4 is the richest player with $1542 and a full light blue set. p1 actually owns only two of the three pink properties, missing Virginia Avenue.

I just paid $10 rent on St. Charles Place. p3's Boardwalk and Park Place each have one house, so their rent is $200 and $175. They cannot afford to build more houses because they only have $222 cash.

I cannot complete a property set without bankrupting myself. A second house on Boardwalk costs $600, and I would need $400 more to even up with p3. I will stay liquid and avoid funding opponents.

No trade can complete a monopoly for me right now. The missing pieces are unowned. p3 will not sell his dark blue set. p1 does not own a complete set.

A light blue monopoly would cost roughly $320 in cash. p4 has $1542 and will not sell both light blue properties cheaply. Acquiring them would require two trades and would strengthen p4. That is not worth the risk.

I should not trade Ventnor back to p4. That would give them two of three yellow properties. I also will not give p1 cash to buy Virginia. That would complete their pink monopoly against me. I have no reason to mortgage anything.

I will end the turn. Mortgaging would reduce rent collection and add interest costs to unmortgage later.

I considered trading with p3 to break his dark blue monopoly. He would never accept Ventnor, Penn, and cash for Boardwalk or Park Place because those are his win condition. I should not offer him that much money if he rejects the deal.

I rejected a specific trade with p4: offering Penn for Marvin would leave me with only two yellow properties, not a complete set. I will avoid proposing any trade that helps an opponent or reveals my strategy.

I just realized my previous trade with p4 was a mistake. I gave away Marvin Gardens and Reading Railroad for Ventnor Avenue and Pennsylvania Avenue. Pennsylvania is green, not yellow, so that swap never completed a color set.
